clue.text: Reviewing crime scene in play

definitions.note: a verb form defining a noun: the act of looking back over the past

indicators.note: letters put in play are set moving and rearranged rather than kept in their printed order

parts.note: twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective drama replays the crime scene on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminiscence is a recollection, the mental act of going back over past events and experiences.

clue.text: Leave off — such a burden!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hold back from doing something
second meaning: the recurring chorus of a song, an old sense of burden

explanation.surface: Someone exasperated begs another to stop nagging about a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: Burden here is not a load but the old word for a song's chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to abstain or desist, and a refrain is the repeated lines sung after each verse.

clue.text: Confronts very proper school-head

parts.note: meet is an archaic word for fitting or proper

indicators.note: the head of a word is its leading letter, so only the start is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A strict headteacher squares up to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Meets in the sense of faces or encounters head-on, as when one meets a challenge or opponent.

clue.text: A top figure among mathematicians

parts.note: surface reading: an eminent, leading mathematician
setter's reading: the number written above the line in a fraction

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise for a great mathematician, but the top figure is literally the upper number of a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fraction, the number above the dividing line is called the numerator, the one below the denominator.

clue.text: Rings up repeatedly, but that's tolerable

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are written from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: O is a ring, so rings are Os
the same piece again

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps phoning is a nuisance, though bearable.
explanation.walkthrough: Rings looks like telephoning; it is the plural of the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so is an informal expression for middling, passable, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Raised by a sovereign?

parts.note: surface reading: lifted up or brought up with a gold coin, or by a king
setter's reading: elevated to the peerage by the monarch

explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also a gold coin, which tempts thoughts of money; the sense meant is a monarch creating a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made a lord or lady by the monarch is elevation to noble rank, so the person is ennobled.

clue.text: A Scot taking a break at the seaside

indicators.note: something taking a break is broken up, so the letters are split apart and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman on holiday by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast is the land along the sea, the shore where people go for a seaside holiday.

clue.text: Split due to stuff about English standard

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps itself round the others

parts.note: to sate is to fill up or stuff with food
E is the abbreviation for English
par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: A couple broke up over material about English standards.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate is to divide or part, as split does when used as an adjective for things kept apart.

clue.text: A heavy mallet for a six-footer's use

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a heavy wooden hammer for ramming or flattening
second meaning: an insect, since insects have six legs

explanation.surface: A big hammer is offered to a very tall person.
explanation.walkthrough: Six-footer suggests a tall man; it means a creature with six feet, an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a pounding tool used by pavers and an insect order with hard wing cases.

clue.text: Prodigal son embracing mother he's pledged to give assistance

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so these words wrap around another

parts.note: a prodigal is free with money, lavish
taken as written
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A returning wastrel hugs his mother, who has sworn to help him.
explanation.walkthrough: Prodigal son reads as the parable's figure, but the two words are split: prodigal gives one piece, son another, and mother sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons swear oaths in their lodges to aid fellow members, a fraternity built on mutual help.

clue.text: A sharp ridge requiring some care — terribly dangerous

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words
surface padding completing the phrase terribly dangerous

explanation.surface: A climber warns that a knife-edge mountain ridge needs caution as it is very dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: An arete is a narrow mountain crest between two glacial valleys, a knife-edged ridge.

clue.text: Guarantee for a vessel going by river

parts.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Insurance cover for a ship travelling by river.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure is to promise or pledge confidently that something is so, a verbal guarantee.

clue.text: Rating quarter plot of land impractical

parts.note: a rating is an ordinary sailor, and AB is an able seaman
south is one quarter of the compass
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: An assessment finds a quarter-acre plot of no practical use.
explanation.walkthrough: Rating looks like a valuation; in crosswords it often means a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract ideas are theoretical and detached from concrete reality, hence impractical.

clue.text: Lack of clothes can lead to untidy appearance

indicators.note: can lead to signals that the following letters are turned into something new by rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Going without clothes makes one look scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: Untidy looks like the adjective in the surface, but its six letters are what get rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudity is the state of being naked, of wearing no garments at all.

clue.text: Being nice about plug falling off

indicators.note: about here means around, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: decent is nice, pleasant
a plug is a piece of advertising, an ad

explanation.surface: Someone is pleasant about an electrical plug coming loose.
explanation.walkthrough: Plug suggests the electrical fitting; it is a promotional mention.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes something in moral or cultural decline, in a state of falling off from former standards.

clue.text: Become less smooth?

definitions.note: read whimsically as de-crease, to remove creases
definitions.meaning: second meaning, punning: to take out the creases

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: split the word as de-crease and it means ironing out wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: To decrease is to shrink or diminish, and the pun treats it as removing folds to flatten fabric.

clue.text: Soldiers prevail in revolt, causing a suspension

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: things in revolt are overturned and disordered, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A military mutiny succeeds and operations are halted.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieval is a reprieve, a postponement or temporary stay of punishment.

clue.text: Carefree daughter given black look

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
ebon is a poetic word for black
an air is an appearance or manner

explanation.surface: A happy-go-lucky girl receives a dark stare.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means confident, charming and light-hearted, with a breezy untroubled manner.

clue.text: The person scoring for just one instrument

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who keeps the score or record

explanation.surface: A composer writes a score for a single instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoring suggests composing music; it means keeping a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorekeeper or official note-taker is a recorder, and the recorder is also a simple wooden flute.

clue.text: A holiday centre should be concerned with variety

parts.note: re means regarding
a sort is a kind or variety

explanation.surface: A holiday camp ought to offer lots of different activities.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a place people visit for recreation and vacations, such as a seaside town.

clue.text: A very quiet auditor, or so it would seem

parts.note: taken as written
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very soft
the ear is the organ that hears

explanation.surface: A listener seems to be extremely silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditor suggests an accountant; here it is simply a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe giving an outward impression, as in the idiom it would appear, used when judging by evidence.

clue.text: A note newsmen hold back

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
the press are journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Journalists suppress a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to restrain or suppress, keeping feelings or information in check.

clue.text: Point to publication's incitement to riot

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
an edition is an issue of a publication; the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a magazine is stirring up unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is speech or conduct encouraging rebellion against lawful authority.

clue.text: Knocking off an article on little feet

parts.note: the is the definite article
ft is the short form of feet; on places it after

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about tiny feet is being finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Knocking off is British slang for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking off something is informal for stealing it, so the act is a theft.

clue.text: Dr Proudie, for example, having a drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Dr Proudie is the ... in Trollope's Barchester novels
second meaning: a mulled, spiced wine

explanation.surface: A doctor has a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr suggests a medical doctor; Proudie is a churchman with a doctorate of divinity in Trollope's fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Proudie is the Bishop of Barchester, and bishop is also hot port spiced with oranges and cloves.

clue.text: Fellow greeting Roman swell

parts.note: he is a male person
ave is the Latin word of greeting

explanation.surface: A man greets a dapper Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: Swell looks like a fashionable gent; it is the rise and fall of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The heave of the sea is its rising surge, the same motion as a swell of waves.

clue.text: Left in over-large home

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: fat is overweight, too big
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone has been left alone in a house that is too big.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is an apartment, a set of rooms on one floor where people live.

clue.text: The extent of the cooking facilities

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the scope or span

explanation.surface: Someone asks how much cooking equipment there is.
explanation.definitionFit: Range means the scope something covers, and also a large cast-iron kitchen stove with ovens.

clue.text: Blunt centre-half scoffed about vile foul

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only its inner letters are kept

parts.note: its two middle letters

indicators.note: foul suggests something messed up, so the letters are put into a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A blunt-speaking football centre-half sneered at a nasty foul.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre-half is a football position, but it means the middle of the word half. About only joins, as in concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: To blunt pain or distress is to dull or ease it, which is what alleviate means.

clue.text: Spinners of stretchable yarns?

parts.note: surface reading: people spinning elastic thread in a mill
setter's reading: tall tales that stretch the truth, spun by talkers

explanation.walkthrough: Spinning yarns suggests textile work; to spin a yarn is to tell a tale, and a stretched one is exaggerated.
explanation.definitionFit: People who spin tales, exaggerating as they go, are narrators of stories, so tellers of tall tales.
